hero.title: What does a dollar really cost?
hero.body: In much of the world the official exchange rate is not the rate anyone gets. This measures what people actually pay for a dollar — the kind an ordinary person can buy on their phone — in {count} currencies, every hour. Where there is no price, it says so, and why.

howItWorks.dollarCostTitle: What a dollar costs: the price of the stablecoin, divided by the official rate
howItWorks.dollarCostBody: Every hour we price the stablecoin in each country on the exchange people there actually use: Upbit in Korea, Bitso in Mexico, Bitkub in Thailand, about 40 in all, plus Binance P2P where no local exchange works. We take the middle price of the 10 cheapest sellers and divide it by the official rate. The number you see is the median of the last 24 hours. A country with fewer than 10 sellers gets no price, and we say why. The official rate comes from open.er-api.com, a free daily currency feed, with frankfurter.app as a backup and a country's own central bank when one publishes its own number, like Argentina's for the peso. We price the stablecoin because it is the digital dollar people in these countries actually buy and sell. Other coins barely trade there.

roles.heading: Each agent has one job and cannot do the others'
roles.answer: The builder cannot merge its own work. The reviewer cannot write features. The planner never writes code.

items.text: Pulls prices from exchanges, Binance P2P and providers, and writes them to the data files.
Builds exactly one task, then stops. If a task would break a rule, it refuses and flags it.
Checks each change against one question: would this survive a payments expert checking one figure by hand?
Decides what gets built next, and reports what happened. Never writes code, never merges.

incidents.heading: When the agents got it wrong, and the rule each mistake left behind

items.text: It pointed at a hostname that didn't exist. Rule: no collector goes live until it has run once by hand, and silence counts as a failure.
items.what: A collector ran for 34 days and recorded nothing

items.text: A config change put the metered key where the agents' flat-rate key belonged, and it spent real money before anyone noticed. Rule: the two keys live in separate files that cannot be merged.
items.what: A paid key ran the whole system for twenty minutes

items.text: A new data file was not on the list of files to save, and the whole pipeline stopped. Rule: every file is named in the save step, and anything missed is caught and saved with a warning. The gap stays visible in the history.
items.what: 21 hours of prices were lost for good

receiptCrossover.title: The receipt behind this number
receiptCrossover.evidenceSentenceTemplate: {n} real samples at this size, collected between {first} and {last}. The best other app's typical cost across those same hours was {baseline}.
receiptCrossover.feeSentenceTemplate: At {volume} a month, Independent Reserve's own published tier table drops its fee to {feeIr}, and Coins.ph's drops to about {feeCoins} — it varies slightly sample to sample, since it's based on each sample's own real prices.
receiptCrossover.reconstructionNote: This number was never watched happening — it is rebuilt from every real sample's own real prices, swapping in only the fee this volume would unlock.

receiptCrossover.searchSentenceTemplate: We tested monthly amounts from {lo} to {hi} and narrowed in on the exact point where that rebuilt cost first drops below the best other app's typical cost: {volume} a month.

tape.title: What people pay for a dollar, updating every {minutes} minutes
tape.lede: Each row shows what people pay, the official rate, and the difference. Prices are in each country's own currency per US dollar, marked by its three letter code, such as AFN for the Afghan afghani. Central Africa and West Africa are groups of countries that share one currency. The difference is how much more people pay than the official rate, as a percentage. A minus sign means they pay less.
tape.statusIdleLate: The last check is older than {minutes} minutes. This is not a fault. A check may be running or late. The prices shown are from the last check, at the time above.
tape.statusLive: Connected. New prices appear here as each check finishes.
tape.statusOffline: Not connected, so prices may be out of date. Next check at {time} UTC.
tape.statusOfflineLate: Not connected. The last check is older than {minutes} minutes. A check may be running or late. The prices shown are from the last check, at the time above. Reload to try again.
tape.metaTemplate: Last checked on {date} at {time} UTC. {n} countries priced.
tape.unavailable: The latest prices could not be loaded. Try again in a few minutes.
tape.note: Stablecoins are digital coins worth one US dollar each. People trade them with each other on Binance, a large online marketplace. The middle price they ask is what we show as what people pay. The official rate is the bank rate at that moment. A gap means people do not actually get the official rate when they swap money.
tape.linkText: See each country's price over time →
tape.footer: The first two numbers in each row come from the latest check. The difference is worked out from those two.

receiptBasis.title: Where this price comes from
receiptBasis.evidenceSentenceTemplate: {n} people were buying and selling US dollar stablecoins for {ccy} when this was checked: a median buy price of {buy} and a median sell price of {sell}.
receiptBasis.rateSentenceTemplate: The bank rate for {ccy} at the same moment: {rate} {ccy} per dollar.
receiptBasis.rateUnavailable: No bank rate was available for {ccy} at this check.
receiptBasis.mathSentenceTemplate: Street price = the midpoint of the buy and sell medians = ({buy} + {sell}) / 2 = {mid} {ccy}.
